description:
What Happens If You Cry in Space?

Without gravity, tears don't fall. They gather into a wobbly ball of water on your eye, and they sting.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#astronaut #space #iss #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: What happens if you cry in space?

visual.query: ISS-68 NASA astronaut Frank Rubio peers through a window in the cupola
commons: ISS-68 NASA astronaut Frank Rubio peers through a window in the cupola

segments.text: On Earth, tears roll down your cheeks because gravity pulls them.
segments.headline: Gravity pulls tears down

segments.text: In orbit, everything is falling together, so your tears don't fall at all.
segments.headline: Nothing falls

segments.text: Instead, they pile up on your eye, forming a growing ball of water that clings to you.
segments.headline: A ball of water on your eye

segments.text: Astronauts say it stings. Chris Hadfield showed it on video in 2013, and it looks really uncomfortable.
The fix? Wipe it away with a towel, or shake your head and chase the tiny floating drops.

visual.query: Astronaut Jessica Watkins is pictured eating a meal
commons: Astronaut Jessica Watkins is pictured eating a meal

segments.headline: Wipe it away
